newsitem.title: UK: Major calls UK Conservative split talk "off-beam".
newsitem.headline: Major calls UK Conservative split talk "off-beam".

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Friday dismissed as old and "off-beam" reports in two British newspapers that up to 40 pro-European Conservative members of parliament were considering splitting from the ruling party.

The reports said the MPs were threatening to break away and back Labour over Europe if the Conservative leadership fell into the hands of "Euro-sceptic" Defence Secretary Michael Portillo after the coming election.
Speaking in his Huntingdon constituency in eastern England, Major said: "It's a story that has emerged from time to time, usually without any names and has usually been denied by people in the past.
"It seems to have re-emerged, but it's completely off-beam as far as I am aware and there's nothing to justify it."
Major said the government's policy on the European Union's planned single currency, reaffirmed by cabinet on Thursday, was in the national interest.

Ministers formally reaffirmed their wait-and-see stance toward monetary union but effectively ruled out Britain's participation by saying they thought it was very unlikely that the single currency could be launched safely in 1999.

Asked whether he was surprised that the hardline stance had not won over all Conservative "Euro-sceptics" opposed to closer integration, Major replied: "You make an assertion I don't intent to comment upon."

The Daily Mail and the Sun said the breakaway group of pro-European rebels would be named the European Democrats and would be led by either Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke or Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine.

The reports are the latest evidence of feverish jockeying among Conservative MPs predicated on the assumption that the party, well behind in the polls, will lose the coming election and that Major will then step down as leader.
